_comment: Terms that must never reach an Apple App Store Connect note field
(App Review guideline 2.3.10). Consumed by
sanitize_apple_store_notes.py and by the beta_changelog backstop in
ios/fastlane/Fastfile and macos/fastlane/Fastfile, so the two can never
drift apart.
Order is significant: the longest spelling of an overlapping pair is
declared first, so 'Google Play Store' is consumed whole rather than
leaving a stray 'Store' behind.
That rule is what fixes the position of the bare '\bLinux\b' entry.
Every distro whose name contains Linux as a separate word (Arch Linux,
Rocky Linux, Linux Mint, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, ...) is declared
above it, or the bare entry would eat the Linux half and strand the
distro name; every single-word spelling of one of those distros (Arch,
Mint, Red Hat) is declared below it, so the longer spelling always wins.
AlmaLinux is exempt from both halves: there is no word boundary between
Alma and Linux, so the bare entry cannot match inside it.
Windows, PC and Microsoft are case-sensitive on purpose. Across every
file in docs/releases/, capitalised Windows is the operating system and
lowercase window/windows is a UI window or a time window.
Arch and Mint are case-sensitive for the same reason: lowercase 'arch'
is the usual abbreviation for a CPU architecture and 'mint' is ordinary
prose, while the distro is always capitalised. Distro names that are
unambiguous English non-words (Fedora, Gentoo, Manjaro, ...) stay
case-insensitive so a lowercased package-name spelling is still caught.
Distros whose short name is a common word or a plausible dive-site name
(Rocky, Alpine, Kali, Void, MX) are only matched in their
'<name> Linux' spelling, never on their own.
The dnf/yum/zypper entry mirrors the apt one: those are only banned in
command context, because 'yum' is also ordinary prose. pacman and the
package suffixes .deb and .rpm are distinctive enough to stand alone,
the same way .exe and .msi already do.
Patterns use only the regex subset common to Python re and Ruby Regexp:
\b boundaries and (?: ) non-capturing groups. No named groups, no
lookbehind. JSON \b is a backspace, so every boundary is written \\b.
Use [ \t] for whitespace inside a multi-word term, never \s. Release
notes are wrapped Markdown, so 'Google Play' can straddle a line break;
\s would match that newline and the replacement would join the two
lines, breaking the line-count invariant the --report diff depends on.
